question: On what basis does this teaching claim that the cakra in question is rarer than any yoga taught as a standard of comparison?
premises: This cakra is affirmed to be hard to obtain.
There is no yoga that stands as its equal or standard above it in the stated comparison.
The fused comparative marks a relation of superiority to 'this' without positing another named yoga as higher.
inference: The verse makes a superlative claim of rarity: the cakra is not merely difficult, but has no higher yoga as a point of comparison within the scope of this instruction.
uncertainties: The precise referent of 'this cakra' is not recoverable from these seven tokens alone.
It is uncertain whether 'yoga' here means a general discipline or a specific named yoga in this lacunose chapter.
plain_english: Indeed, this circle is hard to obtain; there is no yoga higher than this one.
